There is no fixed number of IVF cycles needed to conceive, though most women succeed within two to three attempts, with cumulative success rising further with each additional cycle. Age, embryo quality and underlying diagnosis all influence this timeline. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai provides IVF Treatment in Mumbai, reviewing and adjusting the protocol after each cycle rather than repeating the same approach unchanged.

Endometrial thickness affects whether an IVF transfer can proceed, with the accepted minimum at 7 mm and the strongest implantation rates typically between 8 and 12 mm. Below that range, pregnancy rates fall noticeably. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai provides IVF Treatment in Mumbai with close attention to lining thickness and pattern, postponing a transfer rather than proceeding before preparation is adequate.

Male infertility contributes to nearly half of all conception difficulties, yet it often goes unevaluated for years while attention stays focused on the woman. Conditions like azoospermia where no sperm are present in semen can still be addressed through surgical sperm retrieval and ICSI. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai assesses male fertility as part of couple-focused care at an IVF centre in Mumbai with a thorough, evidence-based approach.

IVF, or In Vitro Fertilisation, involves controlled ovarian stimulation with daily hormone injections over 10 to 14 days, ultrasound-guided egg retrieval under sedation, laboratory fertilisation through conventional IVF or ICSI, embryo culture for 3 to 5 days, and transfer of the selected blastocyst into the uterine cavity. A blood test confirms implantation 10 to 14 days later. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, who provides IVF Treatment in Mumbai, adjusts the protocol to each patient's specific diagnosis and ovarian response.

IUI places prepared sperm directly into the uterus timed to ovulation — fertilisation occurs naturally inside the body. IVF retrieves eggs, fertilises them in the laboratory, and transfers an embryo. IUI success rates run 10–20% per cycle; IVF reaches 40–60%. For mild male factor, PCOS, or unexplained infertility under 35 with open tubes, IUI is a clinically sound starting point. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai offers both IUI Treatment in Mumbai and IVF Treatment in Bandra West, selecting the approach based on diagnosis, age, and semen parameters.

PCOS is the most common cause of anovulatory infertility — elevated androgens and insulin resistance disrupt the hormonal signals that trigger ovulation, resulting in irregular or absent cycles and fewer real conception opportunities each year. Letrozole has replaced clomiphene as the first-choice ovulation induction medication for PCOS. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, who provides Fertility Treatment for PCOS/PCOD in Mumbai, follows a stepwise approach starting with lifestyle modification before any medication is introduced.

IVF pregnancies carry a modestly elevated gestational diabetes rate  approximately 10–15% compared to 5–9% in spontaneous conception attributed largely to underlying conditions such as PCOS and advanced maternal age rather than the IVF procedure itself. Frozen embryo transfers using hormone replacement protocols show a slightly higher GDM association than natural-cycle transfers. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, whose practice includes an IVF hospital in Mumbai, incorporates metabolic screening into pre-cycle planning for high-risk patients.

A minimum endometrial thickness of 7–8 mm is generally required before an embryo transfer — thinner lining is associated with lower implantation rates and higher miscarriage risk. Causes include inadequate oestrogen stimulation, poor blood flow, intrauterine adhesions, and prior uterine procedures. Interventions such as oestrogen supplementation, sildenafil to improve blood flow, and hysteroscopic adhesion removal are used depending on the underlying cause. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, at an IVF hospital in Mumbai, evaluates endometrial response as a standard pre-transfer step.

Family planning and fertility treatment are frequently approached as a female responsibility, despite male factor infertility contributing to nearly 50% of all cases. Semen analysis, hormonal evaluation, and genetic testing for male partners are as clinically essential as female workup — yet they are often delayed or skipped entirely. featured_reviews.name: Nishant Mhatre
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our journey toward parenthood was not an easy one and like many couples in Mumbai, we found ourselves surrounded by countless IVF and fertility centres almost one in every locality. However, what truly distinguishes Ankoor Fertility Clinic from the rest is that, unlike many clinics that often feel driven primarily by commercial motives, this institution is driven by passion, integrity and genuine care for patients.

Before visiting Ankoor, my wife and I had already consulted two other gynecologists. Our previous experiences felt largely procedural, where treatments seemed to follow a fixed medical playbook with little effort to understand us as individuals. Meeting Dr. Kedar Ganla was a completely different experience altogether.

What impressed us most was his extraordinary dedication and depth of involvement in understanding every aspect of our lives not just our medical reports. He carefully studied our medical history, lifestyle, dietary habits, stress levels, routines and even patterns that we ourselves had overlooked. His approach was deeply analytical yet profoundly humane.

In many other fertility centres, we felt IVF would have been immediately recommended as the default solution. However, Dr. Kedar Ganla was remarkably honest with us. He explained that even if IVF were attempted immediately, the chances of success would remain low unless we first addressed certain health and lifestyle concerns. More importantly, he reassured us that, in his professional opinion, we did not necessarily require IVF at all. He believed that with disciplined lifestyle changes, proper diet, exercise, weight management, and medication, natural conception was genuinely possible for us.

He gave us clear health goals and monitored our progress rigorously during every consultation. In fact, he often reminded us like a strict yet caring school headmaster about the importance of discipline and consistency. At times he even scolded us for not following instructions properly, but today we realise that his firmness came from sincere concern and commitment toward our success. Sometimes, especially in one’s mid and late thirties, that kind of accountability becomes necessary.

The day we discovered that we had conceived naturally was one of the happiest and most emotional moments of our lives. We immediately remembered Dr. Kedar’s words when he confidently told us, “You will be able to conceive naturally.” and indeed, we did.

That, however, was only the first milestone of our pregnancy journey. There were additional complications and concerns during the pregnancy, many of which we may not fully understand technically even today by us. But throughout the entire journey, we placed complete trust in Dr. Kedar Ganla and Dr. Manjusha Ganla. They, along with their entire team, stood firmly beside us not only until delivery, but even during the post-pregnancy phase with unwavering support and care.

This review is not written for promotion, nor is it generated artificially. It comes from genuine gratitude and heartfelt appreciation. We simply wish to recommend and endorse doctor who practise medicine not merely as a profession, but as a passion and a responsibility toward human life.

We will always remain thankful to Dr. Kedar Ganla, Dr. Manjusha Ganla and the entire team at Ankoor Fertility Clinic for helping us achieve one of the greatest blessings of our lives.
